London, United Kingdom410 contributions

The KOTO Experience
Sep 2019
A lovely venue, with the right ethos to "Know One, Teach One" (KOTO) - in the process, helping under-privileged and disadvantaged youth aspire to a career in the hospitality sector, thus transforming their lives, their families, and their communities too. 

A delicious, set menu was provided for our group - with 4 starters, 3 mains, and a tiramisu dessert to finish off the meal. Hence, an interesting mix of traditional Vietnamese, South-East Asian and Western cuisine. All fresh ingredients, and a range of herbs and spices were used with the dishes to help bring out the flavours even more so. A lovely, warm ambiance, supplemented by the great attention provided by the waiting staff, made this a memorable evening for us all.

Meaningful cause
Sep 2019
We ate at Koto in Ho Chi Minh city and most of the Asian main courses we ordered were very delicious, although the quality of their salads and starter rolls could be improved upon and quite a few items we wanted on the menu was not available. The desserts were the most memorable in my opinion. We had a great time and service was very friendly.Their good cause is definitely the highlight as the restaurant also serves as a hospitality training facility for young people from difficult circumstances. I would recommend this restaurant as it does have good dishes and deserves more support to maintain its humanitarian cause.

Lower Hutt, New Zealand37 contributions

Good food for a good cause
Sep 2019 • Couples
We ate at each of Koto's two Hanoi restaurants three years ago and they were fantastic so we headed here with high expectations. It wasn't as good as we remembered Hanoi being, but was still very worthwhile. Koto (Know One, Teach One) was founded 20 years ago by Jimmy Pham, Vietnamese Australian, to teach street kids hospitality skills, and now has 2,000 graduates, so it's worth supporting. The food was good but not memorable (and the meat rather fatty), and the service attentive. There were a couple of big groups in when we arrived, and it would probably work better for groups.

reviews.review_text:
Giao
9 contributions

Better than best
Sep 2019
Only VND400,000 for a three-course lunch for four people. Delicious. I had some real joy chatting with two of the staff members there. Ms. Giang, who received her KOTO training in both Hanoi and Saigon, was very knowledgeable about the restaurant and its associated training center. Jimmy Pham, KOTO's founder, happened to be there when we were finishing our meals -- so we had a crash course on how to do good well. What a blast! My only complaint is it was so empty -- there were only six customers in total during the entire two hours we were there. Saigon's 10 million people should all go here for lunch.
